title: Light and Darkness, Day and Night
notes: This chunk delivers a dense, law-positive chain that equates light with the lived commandment and visible good works, darkness with deliberate concealment of evil, and day/night with the open versus hidden life. Scripture links (Proverbs, Isaiah, John, Exodus plague, Thessalonians, outer darkness) assemble cleanly with the oil/garment symbols and close the chapter without loose ends. Two author-prose sentences violate the house ban on opening with That/And. The rest of the prose is already tight, free of director cues, AI stock, and quote corruption; only those sentence-open fixes are required.

proposals.old: That is why a hidden lamp is no lamp at all — __“neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel”__ (Matthew 5:15).
proposals.new: A hidden lamp is no lamp at all — __“neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel”__ (Matthew 5:15).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with That. The shortened assertion still follows directly from the preceding claim about visible good works and keeps the Matthew citation intact.

proposals.old: And the LORD Himself is source and sum: __“The LORD is my *light* and my *salvation*”__ (Psalm 27:1) — light and _yeshuah_ in one breath.
proposals.new: The LORD Himself is source and sum: __“The LORD is my *light* and my *salvation*”__ (Psalm 27:1) — light and _yeshuah_ in one breath.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with And. Removing the conjunction leaves the same identity claim and the Psalm quotation unchanged.
